title: Best IB Resources for Oxbridge and Ivy League…
summary: Compare the best IB resources for Oxbridge and Ivy League applicants, covering predicted grades, subject depth, admissions tests, and EE preparation.
body_markdown:
Applying to Oxford, Cambridge, or an Ivy League university requires more than completing large quantities of revision. The best IB resources for Oxbridge and Ivy League applicants help produce sustained academic evidence: strong predicted grades, excellent performance in relevant Higher Level subjects, genuine subject depth, and carefully developed coursework.


The requirements are not identical. Oxford and Cambridge publish course-specific academic expectations and may use admissions tests, written work, and interviews. Ivy League universities set separate admissions policies and generally review grades, curriculum, testing, recommendations, essays, activities, and educational context.


### What highly selective universities require


The first step is to separate official requirements from general advice. A resource is useful only if it helps you meet the expectations of your chosen course and institution.


Application factor Oxford and Cambridge Ivy League universities


IB grades Published course-specific expectations, including overall points and HL grades No shared Ivy League IB cutoff


Subject choice Required or recommended subjects are often specified Rigour and preparation matter, but expectations vary


Predicted grades Used when final results are unavailable Often submitted for examination-based curricula


Admissions tests Required for certain courses Testing policies differ by institution and cycle


Written work Requested for some courses Essays are standard, while graded work varies


Interview Academic assessment for shortlisted Oxbridge applicants Availability and purpose differ by university


Activities Academic suitability is central Activities and personal qualities may inform broader review


### Oxford and Cambridge IB requirements


For **2027 entry** , Oxford states that IB applicants need **38, 39, or 40 points** , including core points, depending on the course, with **6s and 7s at Higher Level** . Individual courses may require particular HL subjects or grades, so an overall total is not sufficient by itself.


Oxford considers available evidence such as academic achievement, predicted grades, admissions tests, written work, interviews, references, and the UCAS application. Not every course uses every component. Applicants should consult Oxford's[official admissions requirements table](https://www.ox.ac.uk/admissions/undergraduate/courses/admission-requirements/admission-requirements-table) .


Cambridge course pages for **2027 entry** commonly state minimum offer levels of **41-42 points with 776 at Higher Level** , although conditions vary by course and College. Some courses prescribe particular HL combinations. Cambridge Computer Science, for example, requires Mathematics and asks IB students to take **Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches** .


Cambridge assesses academic records, predictions, references, personal statements, submitted work where requested, assessments, contextual information, and interviews. It also explains that extracurricular excellence does not compensate for lower academic potential. Verify details through Cambridge's[course-specific entry requirements](https://www.undergraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/apply/before/entry-requirements) .


### Ivy League requirements are not uniform


The Ivy League is an athletic conference, not a shared admissions system. Its eight universities establish their own testing rules, application requirements, and procedures for international qualifications. There is no official Ivy League IB score requirement applying to all eight.


Current policies demonstrate this variation.[Harvard's application requirements](https://college.harvard.edu/admissions/apply/application-requirements) normally require the SAT or ACT, with alternatives such as predicted or actual IB results accepted in defined exceptional circumstances.[Dartmouth's testing guidelines](https://admissions.dartmouth.edu/apply/testing-policy) allow students attending schools outside the United States to satisfy its testing requirement through predicted or final IB Diploma results, among other options. Policies can change, so check every university during your application cycle.


### The best IB resources by purpose


A selective application does not require the largest possible collection of materials. It requires a coherent system that improves academic performance while preserving time for reading, research, admissions tests, and application writing.


### 1. Official university admissions pages


Official pages are the most important resources because they determine what you must prepare. Create a separate checklist for every course covering:


- Required overall IB points and HL grades
- Required or recommended subjects
- Admissions tests and registration deadlines
- Written work, portfolios, or supplementary forms
- Standardized-testing and English-language policies


Do not assume that one Ivy League university's policy applies to another, or that Oxford and Cambridge expect identical preparation for similarly named courses.


### 2. Syllabus-aligned notes and specifications


Start with the current IB subject guide, school materials, and structured[IB subject resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) matching your syllabus and examination session. Concise notes can repair knowledge gaps, but they should not replace problem solving.


Subject depth means connecting ideas and applying them in unfamiliar situations. A Biology student should interpret evidence and evaluate limitations, not merely recall processes. An English student should move beyond memorized quotations towards defensible interpretation and close analysis.


### 3. A topic-filtered IB Questionbank


The[RevisionDojo IB Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) is most useful when practice is diagnostic. Complete a short set under time pressure, classify each lost mark, revise the specific weakness, and attempt a different set testing the same skill.


Use four error categories:


- **Knowledge:** Relevant content was missing.
- **Application:** You knew the content but could not use it.
- **Communication:** Reasoning, terminology, or structure was unclear.
- **Timing:** Better time allocation would have improved the answer.


This process can improve the evidence demonstrated in classroom assessments and mocks. The platform does not determine predicted grades; your school remains responsible for its prediction process.


### 4. Timed mocks and admissions-test materials


Strong untimed work does not guarantee reliable examination performance. Use subject-specific questions,[IB Predicted Papers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/predicted-papers) , and full mocks to practise pacing, question selection, and recovery after difficult sections.


Predicted papers are practice materials, not forecasts of exact examination content. They should supplement broad syllabus coverage and official materials provided legally through your school. For Oxbridge admissions tests, begin with the official specification and sample papers because IB exam skills do not transfer automatically to the ESAT, TMUA, TARA, LNAT, UCAT, or STEP.


### 5. Flashcards for precise retrieval


[IB Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/flashcards) suit terminology, formulas, definitions, quotations, and recurring distinctions. They are less effective for complete mathematical solutions, scientific evaluation, or extended analysis.


Keep cards narrow and testable. After recalling information, apply it in a problem or analytical paragraph so that retrieval supports higher-order thinking.


### 6. Criterion-based EE and coursework support


The IB defines the **Extended Essay** as a compulsory, externally assessed piece of independent research presented as formal academic writing of up to **4,000 words** . It develops research, disciplinary understanding, analysis, argument, evaluation, reflection, and academic integrity.


An excellent EE does not guarantee admission, and universities do not generally impose a universal EE-grade condition. Its value lies in developing knowledge and academic writing. For Oxbridge written-work requirements, follow the course instructions rather than assuming your complete EE is acceptable.


The[RevisionDojo Coursework Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/coursework-grader) can identify an unfocused question, unsupported claims, weak evaluation, or structural problems. Feedback must preserve your authorship. Never use AI to write submitted text, invent sources, manufacture data, or replace required supervision.


### 7. Jojo AI and human support


Jojo AI is useful for bounded tasks such as explaining why a method fails, comparing interpretations, clarifying a command term, or producing a fresh practice prompt. After receiving help, solve a related problem independently.


A tutor may help when repeated practice does not reveal the cause of a plateau or when an admissions test requires accountability. Human support should develop your reasoning, not produce application essays or assessed coursework.


### How to strengthen predicted grades responsibly


An **IB predicted grade** is an evidence-based estimate produced by the school, not a score students can negotiate. Schools may consider tests, mocks, essays, practical work, coursework progress, consistency, and teacher judgment, but their procedures differ.


Ask each teacher what evidence will be considered and when predictions will be finalized. Then use this cycle:


1. Establish a timed baseline.
2. Identify the two highest-impact weaknesses.
3. Relearn the necessary content.
4. Complete targeted questions without assistance.
5. Take another timed set and record the change.
6. Maintain that improvement across later assessments.


In RevisionDojo's[2026 State of Learning Survey](https://www.revisiondojo.com/research/state-of-learning-survey) of **2,975 students and teachers** , **78.7% of students** reported that their average subject grade increased, with a self-reported average rise of **0.57 points** . These observational findings do not establish that RevisionDojo caused the changes or guarantee an individual result.


### Building subject depth beyond the syllabus


Oxbridge preparation is explicitly course-focused, while Ivy League review usually considers a wider range of academic and personal evidence. In both systems, sustained engagement is more convincing than superficial participation.


Choose one or two meaningful extensions:


- Read an introductory university text, review article, or primary source.
- Follow an open lecture series and record questions.
- Critique an argument, proof, experiment, or model.
- Complete a small project producing genuine analysis.
- Enter a competition when its preparation develops relevant skills.


Keep a notebook recording each source's central claim, method, assumptions, limitations, and your response. This provides stronger interview preparation and more authentic application material than a list of titles you cannot discuss.


### A practical weekly preparation system


Weekly block Main purpose Suitable resources


3-4 focused sessions Strengthen IB subjects Study Notes, Questionbank, school materials


1 timed paper or section Build exam reliability Mocks, official materials, Predicted Papers


2 short recall sessions Retain precise knowledge Flashcards and an error log


1 coursework block Improve EE, IA, or TOK work Official criteria and supervisor feedback


1 subject-depth block Develop course knowledge Academic reading and independent problems


Course-specific blocks Prepare for admissions tests Official specifications and samples


During demanding coursework periods, shorten sessions rather than abandoning exam practice. A focused 30-minute timed set with careful correction is more useful than an unfocused three-hour session.


### Common mistakes competitive applicants make


- **Neglecting required HL grades.** A high total may not satisfy a subject condition.
- **Treating minimum requirements as guarantees.** Selection remains competitive.
- **Using predicted papers as forecasts.** Their purpose is practice and diagnosis.
- **Forcing the EE to match an intended degree.** Feasibility and disciplinary quality come first.
- **Substituting activity quantity for academic preparation.** This is particularly unsuitable for course-focused Oxbridge selection.
- **Submitting AI-generated prose.** This undermines authenticity and may breach applicable rules.
- **Following outdated testing advice.** Verify each university's current policy.


### Conclusion


The best IB resources for Oxbridge and Ivy League applicants support four priorities: meeting exact course requirements, producing credible predicted-grade evidence, developing subject depth, and completing independent work with integrity. Official university pages come first, followed by syllabus-aligned learning, targeted questions, timed practice, and careful feedback.


RevisionDojo can bring these study functions into one system without replacing teachers, supervisors, or official admissions guidance. Start with the Questionbank and subject resources, then add Flashcards, Predicted Papers, the Coursework Grader, or Jojo AI when each addresses a specific weakness.
